name: Mung bean (food medium)
description: Food-derived medium: metabolizable components of Mung bean (Vigna radiata) [Pulses] from FooDB, plus a standard M9 mineral base. Organic components use presence-based uptake bounds; FooDB content retained. Measured compounds with no BiGG exchange are listed under uncovered.

provenance.citation: FooDB v2020-04-07 (Wishart DS et al., foodb.ca). Content sources: DTU, DUKE, PHENOL EXPLORER, USDA.
provenance.notes: Organic components mapped from FooDB compounds to BiGG via InChIKey/name. Mineral base added. Bounds presence-based; foodb_content retained. Unmapped measured compounds kept in uncovered (v2 completeness fix). IMPORTANT: composition values are taken from the archived FooDB 2020-04-07 CSV data release; FooDB's live food page no longer displays this bulk composition, so it will appear empty. Verify individual compounds via the per-component cross-reference links. Underlying content was aggregated by FooDB from USDA / DTU / Phenol Explorer.
provenance.verification: expert-curated (multi-source food composition; growth-relevant profile completed, FooDB noise removed)
curation_sources: USDA FoodData Central FDC 174256 (Mung beans, mature seeds, raw; SR Legacy) - full nutrient panel: sugars, amino acids, fatty acids, minerals, vitamins
Devi et al. 2025, Profiling the Nutritional, Phytochemical and Functional Properties of Mung Bean Varieties, PMC11854456 (phytic acid, oxalate, proximates, amino acids)
Tajoddin & Shinde 2014, The Bioscan (raffinose/stachyose/sucrose contents of mung bean cultivars)
Kuo, VanMiddlesworth & Wolf 1988, J Agric Food Chem 36:32 doi:10.1021/jf00079a008 (raffinose-family oligosaccharides incl. verbascose in seeds)
Ganesan & Xu 2018, Food Sci Human Wellness doi:10.1016/j.fshw.2017.11.002 (mung bean phytochemical review; malic+quinic dominant organic acids)
Guajardo-Flores et al. 2013, Food Chem doi:10.1016/j.foodchem.2012.10.001 (HPLC-UV organic-acid panel of V. radiata sprouts)
provenance.curation_notes: Dry high-protein/high-starch legume seed: the dominant carbon source is starch (~46 g/100g) hydrolysing to glucose, backed by sucrose plus the raffinose-family oligosaccharides (stachyose/verbascose/raffinose) that need α-galactosidase; the dominant nitrogen source is the 23.9 g/100g protein (glutamate- and aspartate-rich, lysine-rich, Met/Cys-limited). Organic acids - entirely absent from the FooDB profile - were added: phytic acid (~446 mg/100g) is quantitatively dominant and also the main P s
curation_added: phytic acid (~446 mg/100g) - dominant organic acid and phosphorus store, absent from FooDB profile
malic + quinic acid (co-dominant organic acids, 55-86% of total), citric, succinic, fumaric, aconitic, oxalic - organic acids missing from FooDB
quantitative free-sugar / RFO split: sucrose ~1.5 > stachyose ~1.0 > verbascose ~1.5 > raffinose 0.53 g/100g
starch (~46 g/100g) - the dominant fermentable carbon reservoir
full amino-acid profile with amounts and total protein (23.86 g/100g)
full vitamin panel with amounts (B1/B2/B3/B5/B6/B9/C/E/K, choline; B12 confirmed absent)
individual fatty acids and total fat

curation_removed.name: Arsenate
curation_removed.reason: toxic metalloid soil contaminant, not a growth nutrient; FooDB trace

curation_removed.name: Retinol
curation_removed.reason: preformed (animal) vitamin A; absent in this plant seed, which supplies only provitamin-A carotenoids; FooDB predicted

curation_removed.name: epsilon-Polylysine
curation_removed.reason: bacterial-fermentation food-preservative polymer, not a native mung bean constituent; FooDB implausible/predicted

curation_removed.name: (±)-erythro-Isoleucine
curation_removed.reason: non-biological D/allo stereochemistry artifact duplicating L-isoleucine; not a real seed metabolite

curation_removed.name: (R)-Oxypeucedanin
curation_removed.reason: furanocoumarin characteristic of Apiaceae/citrus, biologically implausible in a legume seed; FooDB predicted

curation_removed.name: Ascorbigen
curation_removed.reason: indole-ascorbate adduct derived from Brassica glucobrassicin; implausible in a legume (non-Brassica); FooDB predicted

curation_removed.name: (E)-2-Phenyl-2-butenal
curation_removed.reason: trace volatile flavour aldehyde, not a growth nutrient

coverage_source.definition: pct_covered_all = components / (components + unresolved ingredients) — the legacy metric, which counts pipeline-derived components as covered. pct_covered_source = source-stated components / (those + unresolved ingredients + ingredients replaced by derived components). Component classes come from tools/component_evidence_classes.tsv. A null value means the denominator was zero; it does not mean 100.
